order: Bucket review findings by provenance, then close the running-process rule gap. A calibration audit found the reviewer accurate but miscalibrated, because severity did double duty — hardening shortfalls drew MAJOR beside contract violations, while REVISE became near-universal. Make every finding carry a [BREACH] or [GAP] bucket alongside severity, then key the verdict rule on the bucket, so a CRITICAL or MAJOR BREACH forces REVISE while GAPs and MINOR BREACHes permit APPROVE with the findings as backlog. The same probe refuted the protocol document's claim that every command-running role carries the rule against ending a turn on a still-running process; two top-level roles plus the three architect launchers lack it, so give all five that rule and record the change in the changelog and version stamp. Work only on the reviewer brief's finding format and verdict rule, one added rule paragraph per role file, plus those two records, leaving every other line of those files unchanged.
claims: Every finding carries a [BREACH] or [GAP] bucket beside severity, then the verdict rule keys on it, so a CRITICAL or MAJOR BREACH forces REVISE while GAPs and MINOR BREACHes permit APPROVE. The rule against ending a turn on a still-running process was added to all five command-running roles, phrased for each failure shape, but no other line in those files was touched. The changelog entry and the version stamp record the change. The frontmatter lint reports 37 passed, while the installer's lint checked 19 files with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
